## Verdict

wrong

## Bearer

CumulativeDeltaEstimator — core-domain/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/domain/sensor/CumulativeDeltaEstimator.kt

## Trigger

`ProjectionViewModel.computeState`, called from `recompute` on every
mark and every clock tick while the projection screen is shown —
observed

## Today

`CumulativeDeltaEstimator.estimate` looks up the current segment with
`raceSegments.first { it.index == currentSegmentIndex }` (line 22),
with nothing checking the match exists before using it at line 33.
The lookup only succeeds today because `raceSegments` always comes
from `buildSegments` (`SegmentBuilder.kt`), which `require`s exactly
30 entries and always produces indices 1..30 — an invariant enforced
in that file, not visible to `CumulativeDeltaEstimator` or to its
caller, `ProjectionViewModel.computeState`, which passes
`index = heldRace.currentSegmentIndex ?: 1` as `currentSegmentIndex`.
If a caller ever passes a `raceSegments` list without every index (an
incomplete or partially-built list, as already happens for a race
synced from an early-stopped watch — see the sibling gap on
`RaceDetailViewModel`), `first {}` throws `NoSuchElementException`
straight out of `estimate`, uncaught, rather than the function stating
what it returns for that case.

A second, independent case of the same pattern:
`RaceRecordingRepositoryImpl.undoLastMark` — app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/race/RaceRecordingRepositoryImpl.kt,
line 153 — looks up the segment it has just closed with
`race.segments.first { it.index == closedIndex }`, right after
computing `closedIndex = currentIndex - 1` from the race's own
`currentSegmentIndex`. It is safe today for the same reason: `segments`
is always the 30-entry list `buildSegments` produces. Nothing in
`undoLastMark` itself checks the segment exists before reading its
`durationMs`; a `race.segments` list missing that index throws the
same uncaught `NoSuchElementException`. This is a distinct symbol from
`CumulativeDeltaEstimator.estimate` — the fix in one does not reach
the other, since neither follows from the other and each reads a
different list under a different call path.

## Expected

`CumulativeDeltaEstimator.estimate` finds the current segment with a
lookup that does not throw when the index is absent (`firstOrNull`,
or equivalent), and states what it returns in that case — consistent
with the function's existing `CumulativeDeltaResult.Fallback` outcome,
already used for a missing lap delta.

Second gap: `RaceRecordingRepositoryImpl.undoLastMark` needs the same
treatment on its own lookup — finding the closed segment with a
non-throwing lookup and stating what `undoLastMark` returns when the
segment it expects to have just closed is not in the list, rather than
relying on the invariant `SegmentBuilder.buildSegments` happens to
hold today.
